description: DSPy: The framework for programming—not prompting—language models

latest_release.body:
# DSPy 3.5: A Lighter, Faster Foundation

DSPy 3.5 brings a lighter LM layer, graduated core modules, and new History and image capabilities for RLM.

## Upgrading from 3.4.1

**This release changes prompts, defaults and APIs.** Read the [upgrade guide](https://dspy.ai/current/community/upgrading-to-3-5/) for breaking changes, migration steps and compatibility limits, and re-evaluate optimized programs.

## Highlights

### RLM, Flex and GEPA graduate

`dspy.RLM`, `dspy.Flex` and `dspy.GEPA` are no longer experimental.

### ReActV2 now replaces ReAct

ReActV2 is now simply `dspy.ReAct`, with structured History and a typed `submit` tool; the old name is deprecated until 3.6.

### Rich tool results

Tools can return images, files and other DSPy content parts on supported provider routes.

### RLM History — authored by Matt Mannucci (@mannuch)

RLM can save and reload conversation History for later calls; it does not restore live interpreter variables.

### A lighter LM foundation — lm15 work by Maxime Rivest (@MaximeRivest), integration by Isaac Miller (@isaacbmiller)

LiteLLM and OpenAI’s Python library are now optional: DSPy calls supported providers through the lightweight lm15 engine.

| Measured default install | 3.3.0 | 3.5 development snapshot |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Installed package files, including bytecode | 206.7 MiB | 30.9 MiB |
| Dependencies, excluding DSPy | 65 | 25 |
| Fresh-process import, best of ten | 1.01 s | 0.49 s |

### Automatic API-family routing

`model_type="auto"` is the default, rather than explicitly selecting chat or responses.

### XMLAdapter is now the default Adapter

XMLAdapter now formats and parses predictor calls by default, changing prompts and the output contract even when your Signature stays the same.

### Native reasoning and explicit plans

Prefer native reasoning; request an explicit plan when planning before acting helps the task or it needs a human-auditable plan.

### Disk caches: secure by default

Restricted loading is now the default, and plain NumPy arrays are stored without pickle.

### Image-capable RLM

RLM can crop images with Pillow and send mixed text/image subqueries from its Python REPL.

With DSPy imported, an image-capable LM configured and the default Deno runtime available:

```python
rlm = dspy.RLM("photo: dspy.Image, question: str -> answer: str")
result = rlm(photo=dspy.Image.from_path("photo.png"), question="What is written on the smallest sign?")
print(result.answer)
```

**Prewarmed Interpreters**

Real DSPy now runs inside RLM and Flex interpreters, with a precompiled standard library, cached startup snapshots and `InterpreterPool` for prewarming.

| Measured path | 3.4.1 | 3.5 development snapshot |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cached Deno startup + first execution | 1.59 s | 0.45 s |
| DummyLM Flex forward | 1.61 s | 0.63 s |
| Flex with a ready size-one pool | — | 0.10 s |

Medians of nine fresh processes per path, with prepared runtime caches; pool readiness costs another 0.55 s, excluded from the pooled forward. First-use preparation can be slower.

## Full PR List

All 99 PRs in the verified range appear once in the list below. Earlier intermediate bundled-lm15 and metadata updates are included for completeness; the cutoff contains bundled lm15 2.2.0 and metadata sourced from released LiteLLM 1.108.3.

### Language Models, Adapters, and Reasoning

- fix(xml): honor positional tuple schemas by @isaacbmiller ([#10850](https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/pull/10850)).
- fix(adapters): preserve nested XML enum and null guidance by @isaacbmiller ([#10859](https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/pull/10859)).
- Default LM API-family selection to native lm15 routing by @isaacbmiller ([#10856](https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/pull/10856)).
- fix: honor reasoning dictionaries in ChainOfThought by @isaacbmiller ([#10842](https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/pull/10842)).
- fix(xml): pars

detail.readme: ## DSPy: _Programming_—not prompting—Foundation Models **Documentation:** [DSPy Docs](https://dspy.ai/) [![PyPI Downloads](https://static.pepy.tech/personalized-badge/dspy?period=monthly)](https://pepy.tech/projects/dspy) ---- DSPy is the framework for _programming—rather than prompting—language models_. It allows you to iterate fast on **building modular AI systems** and offers algorithms for **optimizing their prompts and weights**, whether you're building simple classifiers, sophisticated RAG pipelines, or Agent loops. DSPy stands for Declarative Self-improving Python. Instead of brittle prompts, you write compositional _Python code_ and use DSPy to **teach your LM to deliver high-quality outputs**. Learn more via our [official documentation site](https://dspy.ai/) or meet the community, seek help, or start contributing via this GitHub repo and our [Discord server](https://discord.gg/XCGy2WDCQB). ## Documentation: [dspy.ai](https://dspy.ai) **Please go to the [DSPy Docs at dspy.ai](https://dspy.ai)** ## Installation ```bash pip install dspy ``` To install the very latest from `main`: ```bash pip install git+https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy.git ``` The current LM integration uses bundled native lm15 engines, without a LiteLLM runtime dependency or fallback. See the [LM migration guide](docs/docs/community/normalized-lm-api-migration.md) for breaking changes to provider options, custom LMs, text completions, and embeddings. ## 📜 Citation & Reading More If you're looking to understand the framework, please go to the [DSPy Docs at dspy.ai](https://dspy.ai). If you're looking to understand the underlying research, this is a set of our papers: **[Jul'25] [GEPA: Reflective Prompt Evolution Can Outperform Reinforcement Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.19457)** **[Jun'24] [Optimizing Instructions and Demonstrations for Multi-Stage Language Model Programs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.11695)** **[Oct'23] [DSPy: Compiling Declarative Language Model Calls into Self-Improving Pipelines](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.03714)** [Jul'24] [Fine-Tuning and Prompt Optimization: Two Great Steps that Work Better Together](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.10930) [Jun'24] [Prompts as Auto-Optimized Training Hyperparameters](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.11706) [Feb'24] [Assisting in Writing Wikipedia-like Articles From Scratch with Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.14207) [Jan'24] [In-Context Learning for Extreme Multi-Label Classification](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.12178) [Dec'23] [DSPy Assertions: Computational Constraints for Self-Refining Language Model Pipelines](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.13382) [Dec'22] [Demonstrate-Search-Predict: Composing Retrieval & Language Models for Knowledge-Intensive NLP](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.14024.pdf) To stay up to date or learn more, follow [@DSPyOSS](https://twitter.com/DSPyOSS) on Twitter or the DSPy page on LinkedIn. The **DSPy** logo is designed by **Chuyi Zhang**. If you use DSPy or DSP in a research paper, please cite our work as follows: ``` @inproceedings{khattab2024dspy, title={DSPy: Compiling Declarative Language Model Calls into Self-Improving Pipelines}, author={Khattab, Omar and Singhvi, Arnav and Maheshwari, Paridhi and Zhang, Zhiyuan and Santhanam, Keshav and Vardhamanan, Sri and Haq, Saiful and Sharma, Ashutosh and Joshi, Thomas T. and Moazam, Hanna and Miller, Heather and Zaharia, Matei and Potts, Christopher}, journal={The Twelfth International Conference on Learning Representations}, year={2024} } @article{khattab2022demonstrate, title={Demonstrate-Search-Predict: Composing Retrieval and Language Models for Knowledge-Intensive {NLP}}, author={Khattab, Omar and Santhanam, Keshav and Li, Xiang Lisa and Hall, David and Liang, Percy and Potts, Christopher and Zaharia, Matei}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2212.14024}, year={2022} } ```
